[Problem]{.card-kicker} **H-Index** [LC 274 · H-Index](https://leetcode.com/problems/h-index/){difficulty="Medium"}

The answer can never exceed $n$, because an h-index of $h$ needs $h$ papers. So a paper with 1000 citations helps exactly as much as one with $n$ citations, and every count above $n$ can be **clamped** to $n$. After clamping, the keys live in $[0, n]$, a range as small as the input, and a counting-sort histogram read from the top answers the question: walk $h = n, n-1, \dots$, keep a running total of papers with at least $h$ citations, and stop at the first $h$ where that total reaches $h$.

[Solved in full in @sec-lts-p1-c.]{.card-link}

:::
